name: PA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+19 partisan lean makes this one of the most Democratic seats in Pennsylvania
Boyle holds a massive financial edge: $5.6 million cash on hand versus no reported fundraising for Arriaga
Incumbency and established name recognition with no outside spending against Boyle
Prediction markets price Boyle's win at roughly 96 percent
model.rationale: A D+19 district, an entrenched incumbent with a multi-million-dollar cash advantage, and a challenger with no reported fundraising leave little basis for doubt; fundamentals and markets alike point to a wide Boyle victory.
model.watch: With no polling in the race and a low-profile challenger, only a sudden scandal or unexpected infusion of challenger resources could make this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 2nd District carries a D+19 partisan lean, among the most Democratic in the state. Brendan Boyle, the incumbent, seeks another term with a substantial war chest: he has raised about $2.5 million and holds more than $5.5 million in cash, with no outside spending directed against him. His Republican challenger, Jessica Arriaga, shows no reported fundraising or cash on hand.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and it has drawn little outside attention. Prediction markets price Boyle's chances at roughly 96 percent. The fundamentals — district partisanship, incumbency, and the stark money gap — all point to a comfortable Boyle win, with the real uncertainty concerning the size of the margin rather than its direction.
